problem: Consider a rectangle such that the height is fixed but its base $b$ can vary. What is the best interpretation of ${A}^{′}(b)$ if $A$ is the area of the rectangle?

choices.value: The length of the base of the rectangle
The rate at which the area changes as the base changes

feedback.problem: Consider a sphere such that its volume $V$ can vary. What is the best interpretation of ${r}^{′}(V)$ if $r$ is the length of the radius of the sphere?
feedback.worked_solution:
The function $r(V)$ gives the length of the radius of a sphere with volume $V.$ So,

$$
{r}^{′}(V)=\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}V}=\frac{\text{Change in }r}{\text{Change in }V}.
$$

Therefore, ${r}^{′}(V)$ is the rate at which the radius changes as the volume changes.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The rate at which the radius changes as the volume changes
